newsitem.title: USA: US Treasuries open peppier before GDP, U. Michigan.
newsitem.headline: US Treasuries open peppier before GDP, U. Michigan.

text.p: U.S. Treasuries perked up a bit for the open, ending earlier losses before release of the third and final estimate of first quarter Gross Domestic Product and the University of Michigan consumer confidence index.

"We were seeing a bit of a bid overnight. Mainly it looks like Asian accounts, and it looks like that spurred a little bit of short covering in the (September bond) contract," said Greg Carr, bond market analyst at A.G. Edwards and Sons Inc. "It looks like the dollar is sharply higher as well."
The T-bond opened up 7/32 at 98-7/32 with a yield of 6.76 percent. The 10-year note was 4/32 higher at 101-3/32, yielding 6.47 percent
At 1000 EDT comes the final snapshot on consumer sentiment in June from the University of Michigan. A reading of 103.5 is expected, up slightly from a preliminary 103.2.

Although the Federal Reserve is surely keeping close tabs on the consumer outlook, even a strong number is unlikely to alter expectations of steady policy at next week's two-day FOMC meeting, starting Tuesday, market analysts said.
Besides, it would take a huge number to shock the market after the Conference Board said on Monday its June index of consumer sentiment rose to nearly a 28-year high.
Chris Iggo, chief economist at BZW Securities, said he did not expect a meaningful reaction to the University of Michigan data "unless there is a big revision."

"I think people have still got the Conference Board number in their mind, that the consumer is still very confident, but nobody is expecting anything from the Fed next week," Iggo said. "The next big event will be the payrolls next Thursday."
The dollar rose more than one yen overnight amid backpedaling on rate hike expectations in Japan. It also rose against the mark.
Treasuries were also helped by a bid tone in many overseas bond markets, analysts said.
"I think there was a little bit of buying from overseas," Iggo said. "The JGB market had a pretty good rally overnight and the European markets were kind of mixed but mostly up."
The approach of the quarter's end seemed to facilitate squaring of short positions as well, analysts said.
